people.name: Alan Mathison Turing
people.summary: English pioneer of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence whose wartime codebreaking and foundational work on computation reshaped modern technology.

people.name: Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace
people.summary: Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace, also known as Ada Lovelace, was an English mathematician and writer chiefly known for her work on Charles Babbage's proposed mechanical general-purpose computer, the Analytical Engine. She was the first to recognise that the machine had applications beyond pure calculation and is sometimes considered the first computer programmer.

people.name: Henry II, Holy Roman Emperor
people.summary: Henry II (Saint Henry) was Holy Roman Emperor from 1014 to 1024 and the last ruler of the Ottonian dynasty. Rising from Duke of Bavaria (995), he secured the German throne in 1002, became King of Italy in 1004, and was crowned emperor by Pope Benedict VIII in 1014. A pious ruler closely allied with the Church, he founded the Diocese of Bamberg, promoted monastic reform, and consolidated imperial authority north of the Alps. Dying childless in 1024, he was canonized in 1146.
